5/9:
Below is a short analysis of what’s going wrong and a single patch that fixes the “shell-session” tokenizer by restricting the output‐regex to lines that do not start with a prompt (`$` or `#`) and by turning it into a proper multiline pattern.

1) Bug scenario & root cause  
   - In recent downloads of Prism 1.22+ (and 1.23), the `shell-session` grammar’s `'output'` token is defined as  
       ```js
       'output': /.(?:.*(?:[\r\n]|.$))*/
       ```
     which is overly greedy (and doesn’t use the multiline (`m`) flag). In practice it swallows both your prompts and your commands, so nothing ever gets highlighted as a command.  
   - Originally (in earlier builds) the output‐regex only matched lines that did *not* start with a shell prompt, and was applied in multiline mode.

2) Patch  
   - We replace the simple, greedy regex with a multiline pattern that only matches one or more lines that *start* with a character other than `$` or `#`.  
   - We also change the simple regex value into an object with `pattern: …` and `alias: 'output'` so that Prism can style it with the proper alias.

```javascript
### components/prism-shell-session.js
<<<<<<< SEARCH
\t\t},
\t\t'output': /.(?:.*(?:[\\r\\n]|.$))*/
\t};
=======
\t\t},
\t\t'output': {
\t\t\tpattern: /^(?:[^#$\\r\\n].*(?:\r\n?|\n|$))+/m,
\t\t\talias: 'output'
\t\t}
\t};
>>>>>>> REPLACE
```

Explanation of the new pattern:

• `^`                        – match the beginning of a line  
• `(?:[^#$\r\n].*)`          – ensure the first character is *not* `#` or `$` (nor a newline), then consume the rest of that line  
• `(?:\r\n?|\n|$)`           – match the line ending (or end-of-input)  
• `)+`                       – repeat for as many contiguous output lines as there are  
• `m` flag                   – so that `^` and `$` apply per line  

With this change only non-prompt lines become “output,” and your prompt+command lines fall back into the normal `command` token.
